name: Vus the Cossack and Strings
description: Vus the Cossack has two binary strings, that is, strings that consist only of " 0 " and " 1 ". We call these strings $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. It is known that $$$|b| \leq |a|$$$, that is, the length of $$$b$$$ is at most the length of $$$a$$$. The Cossack considers every substring of length $$$|b|$$$ in string $$$a$$$. Let's call this substring $$$c$$$. He matches the corresponding characters in $$$b$$$ and $$$c$$$, after which he counts the number of positions where the two strings are different. We call this function $$$f(b, c)$$$. For example, let $$$b = 00110$$$, and $$$c = 11000$$$. In these strings, the first, second, third and fourth positions are different. Vus the Cossack counts the number of such substrings $$$c$$$ such that $$$f(b, c)$$$ is even . For example, let $$$a = 01100010$$$ and $$$b = 00110$$$. $$$a$$$ has four substrings of the length $$$|b|$$$: $$$01100$$$, $$$11000$$$, $$$10001$$$, $$$00010$$$. $$$f(00110, 01100) = 2$$$; $$$f(00110, 11000) = 4$$$; $$$f(00110, 10001) = 4$$$; $$$f(00110, 00010) = 1$$$. Since in three substrings, $$$f(b, c)$$$ is even, the answer is $$$3$$$. Vus can not find the answer for big strings. That is why he is asking you to help him.
input_specification: The first line contains a binary string $$$a$$$ ($$$1 \leq |a| \leq 10^6$$$) — the first string. The second line contains a binary string $$$b$$$ ($$$1 \leq |b| \leq |a|$$$) — the second string.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.
